profile.headline: Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
Applied mathematician and software engineer with extensive experience developing state-of-the-art solutions to practical problems

Ph.D. and M.S.  degrees in Applied Mathematics and B.S. degree in Computer Science from the University of Colorado, Boulder

Experience in all stages of software and algorithm development, from original mathematical research; to analysis of market opportunities; to implementation, testing, documentation, and deployment

Excellent oral and written communication skills (multiple publications in top-tier journals, many presentations to customers, conference presentations, teaching experience, etc.)

Significant programming experience in software baselines with several million lines of code

Software development in large (>100 people) and small (2-person) teams

Experience in many programming languages, e.g. C, C++, Fortran, Python, Java, assembly, MATLAB

Parallel computing technologies such as GPUs, OpenMP, Pthreads, and heavyweight processes

Operating systems: Linux/UNIX, Windows

Programming tools: git, ClearCase, subversion, make, etc.

My research interests include using advanced mathematics to solve problems where traditional numerical approaches are computationally infeasible, especially in problems arising from commercial applications in technology, engineering, and science. For example, I have developed a new method for designing highly accurate and efficient digital filters (IEEE Trans. Signal Process., 2012), created an algorithm for fast and accurate numerical light propagation (Proceedings of the Royal Society A, 2013), and constructed efficient representations of high-dimensional seismic data using simultaneous geometric and Fourier-domain constraints (U.S. patent 9,442,892).

positions.title: Co-Founder and Managing Principal
positions.locationName: Greater Seattle Area and Boulder, CO
positions.description:
Oversaw several projects from initial R&D to profit-generating operations

Created and implemented algorithms for problems as varied as signal processing, machine learning, finance, interplanetary satellite data, and geophysics

Created products using a variety of languages (C, C++, Fortran, Python, and x86-64 assembly) and a variety of technologies (bare metal, AWS cloud computing, GPUs, and multicore OpenMP programming)

Software development lead on multiple projects

Principal Investigator and lead proposal author for SBIR contract with the U.S. Air Force

Ran the business operations of the company, including preparing business models for new products, contract negotiation, and customer interactions

positions.title: NSF IGERT Fellow
positions.description:
Research fellow in NSF-funded program to provide advanced training in computational optics, imaging, and photonics

Research applications include: microscopy, tomography, compressed sensing, spectroscopy, and denoising

positions.title: Research Scientist Intern and Consultant
positions.description:
Introduced a new, compact, representation of seismic data, resulting in U.S. patent 9,442,892

Utilized the new representation to improve the speed and accuracy of algorithms for data interpolation, beam-based migration, and the computation of tau-p (Radon) transforms

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Developed high performance C and C++ software in a Linux/UNIX environment

Designed and implemented signal processing algorithms for offline and real-time systems

Solved problems in application areas including radar pulse detection and characterization, multirate signal processing, cross ambiguity function (CAF) processing, and signal geolocation

Developed software to control microwave-RF transmit and receive hardware for satellite communications

Led small development teams and mentored junior engineers
